title.narrative: NESA/APCSS/BRIN Indo Pacific Minilateral Series: Maritime Security, the Indo-Pacific, and Advancing Maritime Domain Awareness 01-24

description.narrative: The region where the Indian and Pacific Ocean meet is a focal point of maritime security challenges. This program explores how existing cooperative efforts can be made more effective, how institutions focused on maritime security can be founded, how communications regarding shared challenges can be better addressed for the region, and how coordinated maritime effort can discourage provocative actions at sea. The focus is on specific recommendations that aim for efficiency, affordability, political viability, and facilitate partnerships. Specific recommendations will center on the following themes: 1) the ways in which the larger regional maritime community can more commonly interface maritime security efforts, strategic priorities, and training programs; 2) how established methodologies can be merged with new ideas/efforts or operate in parallel with new perspectives to discourage threats; 3) mechanisms to ensure that maritime security discussions do not remain bounded by bureaucratic or institutional silos. The event will be led and hosted by BRIN Center for Political Research and the NESA Center, with DKI APCSS and additional regional partners serving as co-sponsors. The roundtable event will be private in nature, but a public report will be released regarding the conclusions/recommendations crafted over the entire event.
